title: House Floor Debate
subtitle: H.R.1822 — Childhood Education Access and School Choice Act

metadata.laymanSummary: The House passed a school choice bill creating federal education savings accounts worth $10,000 per student annually that families can use at private, charter, or public schools.

data.billTitle: Childhood Education Access and School Choice Act — Creating $10,000 federal education savings accounts for all K-12 students

speakers.name: Rep. Mike Johnson
speakers.title: R-LA · House Speaker
speakers.quote: Every parent in America — regardless of their zip code, their income, or their race — deserves the right to send their child to a school that works. This bill puts parents in charge of their child's education instead of bureaucrats. Competition makes every school better, and every child in America deserves a seat at the best school available to them.

speakers.name: Rep. Hakeem Jeffries
speakers.title: D-NY · House Minority Leader
speakers.quote: This bill takes 90% of its funding from the 50 million children in public schools to benefit the 5 million in private schools. For every $10,000 ESA we fund, we cut $180 from every child who stays in public education. Education reform should lift all ships — not drain the public ocean to fill a private pool.

speakers.name: Rep. Jasmine Crockett
speakers.title: D-TX · House Judiciary
speakers.quote: I grew up in a Title I school. My teachers changed my life with inadequate resources and secondhand textbooks. This bill does not fix those schools — it drains them. The promise of America is not that some children escape bad schools. The promise is that we build good schools for every child, everywhere.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: H.R.1822 passed 222-213, establishing federal Education Savings Accounts worth $10,000 annually per student, usable at accredited private schools, charter schools, or for homeschooling expenses. The Congressional Budget Office estimated the program would cost $72 billion over five years and reduce average per-pupil public school funding by $1,100 in states with declining enrollment.

data.title: Should parents be able to use federal funds at private schools?
